title: Model-View-Presenter

validation.research: Six primary source notes: Potel’s 1996 Taligent publication, Fowler’s GUI Architectures, Passive View, Supervising Controller, his retirement note for his own former MVP entry, and official Python Protocol documentation. Original framework semantics are distinguished from later Passive View teaching code. MVP and Model View Presenter are aliases; MVC/MVVM and the more precise variant names are not silently merged. The assessment-screen second context follows the binding-versus-explicit-update distinction; there is no second runnable GUI implementation.

example_limits: Original sequential in-memory reservation form demonstrating the Passive View variant of MVP. The booking model owns positive whole-seat and capacity rules. The presenter accepts one to three ASCII digits, translates expected BookingError failures into feedback, reads remaining seats, and sends one immutable Screen value to a View render contract. RecordingView stores those values without a model dependency or GUI. It deliberately receives a stale click after Reserve is disabled. The second assessment-screen context illustrates the Supervising Controller tradeoff described by Fowler; it is not a full binding implementation. No GUI event wiring, observers, async work, disposal implementation, persistence, cross-process concurrency, authorization, or rollback is supplied. Unexpected failures propagate; rendering failure does not undo a booking.
